best_for: People who write short plain-text notes and lists on several devices and want free sync without paying or setting up a server.

points.title: Free, sync included
points.text: Apps, sync, backups, sharing and publishing cost nothing. Notes sync on their own as you type, with no sync button to press.

points.title: You must sign in
points.text: There is no local-only mode. The help page says the app cannot be used without a Simplenote account; once you are signed in, the apps work offline and catch up when you reconnect.

points.title: Not for secrets
points.text: Notes travel encrypted, but Simplenote says they are not encrypted at rest on its servers. Keep passwords and private records somewhere else.

points.title: Text only, no attachments
points.text: You cannot attach images or PDFs. Markdown notes can show an image only by linking to one already hosted on the web.

points.title: History, sharing and simp.ly pages
points.text: Each change is saved, so you can roll a note back to last week. You can invite others by email to edit a note (they need an account too) or publish a read-only page at a simp.ly link anyone can open.

points.title: Easy to leave
points.text: Desktop apps export all notes as a .zip, and import takes .txt, .md, .json and, on desktop, Evernote .enex files.

points.title: Mac runs a separate app
points.text: Windows and Linux share one open-source Electron app under GPL-2.0, while the Mac app comes from its own repository, so its version number (2.27.1 here) runs ahead of Windows and Linux (2.24.0).

points.title: Downgrades and the Flatpak
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 50 versions, in per-user or machine-wide installers plus zip builds for x64 and x86. macOS and Linux list only the current release. The Flatpak is a community build that Flathub marks as not verified by Automattic.
